summary: Use Tabs to switch between a few peer views of the same content, such as an account’s overview, activity, and details.

useWhen.text: Switch between a few peer views of the same content, such as an account’s overview, activity and details.

from.quote: Use Tabs to switch between a few peer views of the same content, such as an account’s overview, activity, and details.

avoidWhen.text: The choices do something, such as “Pay” and “Cancel”: use Buttons, not tabs.

from.quote: “Pay” and “Cancel” do something; use Buttons.

avoidWhen.text: A tab needs a disabled or loading state: Tabs has neither.

from.quote: Tabs has no disabled or loading state.

anatomy.holds: The tabs, in one row, 16 px apart.

from.quote: Holds the tabs in one row, 16 px apart.

anatomy.holds: A black label: the view on screen now.

from.quote: Black label: the view on screen now.

anatomy.holds: A 2 px gold bar under the selected tab only.

placementAdvice.text: Show the selected tab’s view below the row; the screen keeps the selected tab.

from.quote: The screen keeps the selected tab and shows that view below the row.

placementAdvice.text: When another tab is pressed, the screen swaps the panel; the tabs only report the press.

from.quote: Pressing another tab swaps the panel; the tabs only report the press.

placementAdvice.text: Tabs stretches to the width of its container; each tab is as wide as its label, with 16 px between tabs.

from.quote: Tabs stretches to the width of its container.

configuration.text: Pass the tabs as TabItem children: children is required, and each child should be a TabItem.
Put each TabItem directly inside Tabs: Tabs passes its modes to direct TabItem children, and does not recognise wrappers or fragments around them.

from.quote: Wrappers and Fragments around TabItems are not recognised.

configuration.text: Set modes on Tabs: they reach its direct TabItem children (not through wrappers or Fragments), and a TabItem's own modes win.
Turn on scrollable when the labels don’t fit, so the row scrolls sideways.

from.quote: Turn on scrollable when the labels don’t fit, so the row scrolls sideways.

configuration.text: Do not squeeze a long set, such as six filters, into a row that doesn’t scroll: every label shrinks and ends in an ellipsis, even “All”.

from.quote: Every label shrinks and ends in an ellipsis, even “All”.

configuration.text: Keep track of the selected tab on the screen: mark that TabItem active, and move the mark when another tab is pressed.

from.quote: The screen keeps track of the selected tab: it marks that tab active and moves the mark when another tab is pressed.

configuration.text: Select exactly one tab: one underline says which view is showing.

from.quote: One underline says which view is showing.

configuration.text: Do not mark two tabs active: only the first is underlined, which may not be the view that’s showing.

from.quote: Only the first is underlined, which may not be the view that’s showing.

rules.text: A few peer views, exactly one selected, and the content below follows it.

from.quote: A few peer views, exactly one selected, and the content below follows it.

rules.text: Name each view in a word or two.

from.quote: Name each view in a word or two

rules.text: Write labels as short nouns in sentence case that name the view, such as “Overview” or “Activity”.

from.quote: Labels are short nouns in sentence case that name the view, such as “Overview” or “Activity”.

rules.text: Don’t number tabs or write actions.

from.quote: Don’t number tabs or write actions.

states.when: The screen opens on the summary view, with the first tab marked active.

from.quote: Open on the summary view.

from.quote: The black label and underline move to the pressed tab.

accessibility.text: On the web the row is a tab list named by its accessibilityLabel, and each tab is announced by its label and whether it is selected.

from.quote: On the web the row is a tab list named by its accessibility label, and each tab is announced by its label and whether it is selected

props.name: children
props.description: Tabs recognises only direct TabItem children; wrappers and fragments around TabItems are not recognised, so they miss the row's modes. Declared: Tab item children. Each child should be a <TabItem> component. Modes are automatically forwarded to all TabItem children.

props.name: modes
props.description: Merged under each direct TabItem child's own modes; the item's modes win. Declared: Design token modes for theming.

props.name: scrollable
props.description: Makes the row a horizontal scroll view: tabs hug their labels 16 px apart, and the row scrolls sideways with no scrollbar or edge hint. Declared: When true, the tabs row scrolls horizontally (useful for many items). Default false, from the component source.

props.name: style
props.description: With scrollable, style lands on the content container, not the viewport. Declared: Override container styles.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Names the tab list on the web. Declared: Accessible name for the tab row.

props.name: testID
props.description: Works since the 636f3f5 build (the 5 October check found none). Declared: Test identifier.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Tab item children. Each child should be a <TabItem> component. Modes are automatically forwarded to all TabItem children.
